newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich says both life, non-life up net.
newsitem.headline: Zurich says both life, non-life up net.

text.p: Swiss insurer Zurich Group credited both life insurance and its bigger non-life business for a 30 percent leap in 1996 net profit to 1.14 billion Swiss francs on Wednesday, at the high end of forecasts.
"The significant increase in annual profit is due to improved performance in both the non-life insurance and life insurance sectors," Zurich said in a statement on 1996 results.
Most analysts' estimates had ranged between 1.08 billion and 1.15 billion net profit.

Zurich said pre-tax profit in non-life insurance, which includes direct non-life business, reinsurance and fund and asset management, rose 14 percent from the year before to 1.44 billion Swiss francs.
"The loss ratio improved despite further strengthening of the loss reserves, qwhile the expense ratio rose not least due to restructuring expenditures," it said.
In life insurance, pre-tax profit shot up 104 percent, mainly due to the acquisition of the U.S.-based Kemper Group but also based on good performance in other operations, the group said.
Gross premiums were 31.9 billion Swiss francs ($21.8 billion), a rise of 7.6 percent in local currencies but 20.5 percent when consolidated in Swiss francs.
"Approximately half of this increase is attributable to the consolidation of additional companies, particularly the Kemper Group in the United States," Zurich said.
It said investment results were again very strong in 1997.
"Overall income from interest, dividends and realised gains rose considerably and exceeded the growth rate of investment," the statement said.
The year-end balance sheet value of investments was 115 billion Swiss francs, up 33 percent. Investments under management totalled 193 billion at year end including assets managed for third parties.
The group's parent company, Zurich Insurance Company, posted a 26 percent jump in net profit to 603.6 million while gross premiums rose 10 percent to 11.5 billion.
